newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African assembly adopts revised constitution.
newsitem.headline: S.African assembly adopts revised constitution.

text.p: South Africa's Constitutional Assembly on Friday overwhelmingly endorsed a revised draft blueprint for post-apartheid rule it hopes to have in place by early 1997.
After three weeks of intense negotiations by political parties, the reworked constitution was adopted by 369 votes against the 326 needed with one vote against and eight abstentions.

The first draft was adopted by an overwhelming majority on May 8, but was referred back by the country's top court for further work on eight shortcomings ranging from an illegal labour relations clause to the inadequate entrenchment of a bill of right.
On Friday, assembly chairman Cyril Ramaphosa said the revised constitution would now be referred back to the Constitutional Court for certification.
"The Constitutional Court has undertaken to give us their judgment as soon as practically possible. If all goes well, implementation of this constitution will begin in a few short months from now.
"But this is not the end of our work. A great task awaits our nation (in) building an appreciation for the values enshrined in this constitution in the eyes of all our people."
The Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party led by Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi boycotted the sitting after last-minute negotiations over the recognition of traditional leaders collapsed on Thursday night.

Inkatha ended an 18-month boycott of the Constitutional Assembly for a week earlier this month, but quit again when their demand for recognition of tribal leaders as the primary local authority in traditional areas was rejected.
The revised constitution contains 42 amendments, two of which were included during the assembly's sitting on Friday.
Most of the amendments were of a technical nature and only 14 involved so-called "substantive" issues.
The Afrikaner-based Freedom Front party abstained from the vote because it believed the constitution failed to meet its demands for self-determination for the Afrikaner nation.
